content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Safety endpoints lack stated analysis methods",
      "quote": "Incidence and severity of adverse events, with severity determined according to the NCI CTCAE v5.0",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoints (AEs, ECOG, vital signs, labs) are listed in Table 4 but no corresponding statistical analysis methods are described in Section 9.3. The statistical analysis section only covers efficacy endpoints (PFS, ORR, OS, DOR, CBR, DCR).",
      "fix": "Add a subsection under Statistical Analyses describing the analysis methods for safety endpoints, including AE incidence, severity grading, and change from baseline summaries."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "PFS, defined as the time from randomization date to the first documented PD, as assessed by investigator according to RECIST v1.1 or death due to any cause, whichever occurs first",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not provide a formal estimand framework. For the primary endpoint PFS, the population (ITT), variable (PFS), and summary measure (hazard ratio) are implied, but intercurrent events (e.g., treatment switching, discontinuation, death without PD) and their handling strategies are not specified.",
      "fix": "Add an estimand section that defines the estimand for each endpoint, including intercurrent event handling strategies (e.g., treatment policy, composite, while-on-treatment)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent analysis of primary endpoint due to early termination",
      "quote": "Following the Sponsor’s decision to prematurely terminate the study, the analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint of PFS will no longer be conducted as per the original study protocol.",
      "page": 81,
      "section": "9.1 Statistical Hypotheses",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol states that PFS will only be analyzed descriptively, but Section 9.3.2 (Primary Endpoint) still describes a formal analysis with log-rank test and Cox model. This inconsistency could lead to confusion in the SAP.",
      "fix": "Update Section 9.3.2 to clearly state that PFS will be analyzed descriptively only, with no formal testing, and remove or revise the inferential methods."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for key secondary endpoints ORR and OS",
      "quote": "ORR, defined as the proportion of participants with a CR or a PR on two consecutive occasions ≥4 weeks apart, as assessed by investigator according to RECIST v1.1",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "ORR and OS are listed as key secondary endpoints, but the statistical analysis section does not provide specific analysis methods for them. Section 9.3.3 (Key Secondary Endpoints) is not present in the extracted text; only general methods for time-to-event and categorical endpoints are given.",
      "fix": "Add a subsection for key secondary endpoints detailing the analysis methods for ORR (e.g., stratified CMH test) and OS (e.g., stratified log-rank test and Cox model)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for additional secondary endpoints CBR and DCR",
      "quote": "CBR, defined as the proportion of participants who experience a best response of SD with a minimum duration of 6 months, a CR, or a PR, as assessed by investigator according to RECIST v1.1",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "CBR and DCR are listed as additional secondary endpoints, but no specific analysis methods are described for them. The general categorical endpoint methods may apply, but the definition of CBR (SD duration ≥6 months) requires time-to-event handling that is not specified.",
      "fix": "Specify the analysis methods for CBR and DCR, including how the 6-month SD duration is assessed and the statistical test used."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing sample size inputs after early termination",
      "quote": "Originally, the sample size of this study was determined by the primary endpoint; therefore, the study was event driven.",
      "page": 81,
      "section": "9.2 Sample Size Determination",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size section only states the original design was event-driven, but does not provide the original assumptions (e.g., expected hazard ratio, median PFS, alpha, power, accrual duration) or the final sample size. This is a gap for regulatory review.",
      "fix": "Provide the original sample size assumptions and the final number of participants enrolled, or state that the study is descriptive and no formal sample size is required."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of missing data",
      "quote": "If a missing category is not presented in the data display, only patients with non-missing values for the parameter being assessed will be included in the percentage calculation.",
      "page": 82,
      "section": "9.3.1 General Considerations",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol only mentions handling of missing categories in categorical summaries, but does not describe how missing data for primary or secondary endpoints (e.g., missing PFS dates, missing response assessments) will be handled in the analysis.",
      "fix": "Add a section on missing data handling, including sensitivity analyses, for all endpoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Multiplicity control not addressed for descriptive analyses",
      "quote": "Accordingly, a control for the overall type I error (α) applying a gate-keeping hierarchical sequential testing method will no longer be implemented.",
      "page": 81,
      "section": "9.2 Sample Size Determination",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The protocol states that no formal testing will be performed, so multiplicity control is not needed. However, it is unclear whether any adjustments will be made for the descriptive p-values or confidence intervals, which could be misleading.",
      "fix": "Clarify that all p-values are descriptive and no multiplicity adjustment is applied, and consider presenting confidence intervals without formal inference."
    }
  ]
}
